method: Original source-face tags retained through Boolean union/difference. Actual per-face colors, no image textures.

rules.name: Unverified closure and model simplification
rules.note: Neutral west closures, opaque room filling and unverified rooflight curb profiles. Not a measured or observed finish.

rules.name: Third-floor overhanging rectangle
rules.note: Three above-ground levels; upper body overhangs north/south, continuous window bands on north/south/east. No mirrored west glazing.

rules.name: First-floor separately traced volumes
rules.note: West rooms, small north meeting volume, southern services and separate eastern glazed pod; circulation between pod and core remains open.

rules.name: Second-floor separately traced volumes
rules.note: West rooms recessed behind north corridor; distinct larger east block, south services and projecting landing; not an extrusion of 1F.

rules.name: North colonnade and structural frame
rules.note: Actual modeled north entry and longitudinal open colonnade; column repetition is simplified.

rules.name: North exterior stair and lift
rules.note: Separate lift shaft and open stair flights/landings; step count and guard widths simplified. No continuous solid stair-core box.

rules.name: South low black canopy and screen
rules.note: Low metal fascia and vertical open bars; not a fourth storey or full added solid wall. Fine bars thickened.

rules.name: Own raised platform and steps
rules.note: Trace-based platform with northeast rounded corner, north/east stairs, southern strip and limited southwest descending entry edge. No lawn or neighboring ramps.

rules.name: Four unequal rooflight footprints
rules.note: One long western and three shorter eastern strips; shallow neutral planar abstraction only. Individual raised/sloped profiles unverified; unlocated AD23 section is not assigned to a strip.

rules.name: Bounded west end and small third-floor landing
rules.note: Stop at B west wall; retain only own shallow west platform and small 3F landing/stair. No L block, glass connector or invented long bridge.
